references.text: Moses spoke these commands and laws to the children of Israel on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, which corresponds to 'on the other side of the Jordan' in Deuteronomy 1:1.
Describes Israel's journeys through the wilderness, including the areas mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:1.
Mentions Hazeroth (חֲצֵרֹת), one of the places referenced in Deuteronomy 1:1.
The Wilderness of Paran is mentioned, corresponding to 'between Paran' in Deuteronomy 1:1.
The Wilderness of Paran is mentioned again in connection with the spies who were sent out.
Israel came to the Wilderness of Sinai, which is part of the same wilderness journey described in Deuteronomy 1:1.
Reiterates that Moses spoke to Israel on the other side of the Jordan, confirming the context from Deuteronomy 1:1.
Moses called all Israel together to speak to them, paralleling Deuteronomy 1:1.
Moses continued to speak these words to all Israel, linking back to the introduction in Deuteronomy 1:1.
Stephen refers to Moses as one who received living words in the wilderness to give to Israel, pointing back to Moses' speech in the wilderness.
